response: Micheál Martin was in Limerick this past week pushing the line that housing tenancies are up, but that line is just a distraction from the real surge in eviction notices and homelessness that followed the government's March 1 rules forcing landlords to offer six-year leases. Nationally the number of people stuck in emergency accommodation has increased again, and it shows how these weak measures do nothing to shield vulnerable groups from the structural inequalities and landlord power that drive the housing crisis. We need urgent, serious reforms to take on the root causes of exploitation and secure stable homes as a basic right instead of letting profits come first—it's long past time to dismantle a system built to serve the powerful at everyone else's expense.
